issuer: the Société de l'assurance automobile du Québec (SAAQ)
note: Read 2026-10-30 on the SAAQ's site (several of its pages answered with a Radware captcha, which wasn't passed; the two used here were served directly, without one). Obtaining a Passenger Vehicle (Class 5) Driver's Licence (updated 9 September 2026): an applicant must be at least 16 (with a parent's consent under 18), a Canadian citizen or authorised to stay more than six months, and resident in Quebec; before holding a full Class 5 licence one holds a learner's licence for 12 months, passes the driving course and the SAAQ's knowledge and road tests, then holds a probationary licence for 24 months. The full licence is so held from 19 (16 plus the two stages): a reading built from the stages, as the page gives no age for the full licence itself. Licence Fees for the Current Year (updated 23 December 2025): Class 5, regular licence, a maximum of $63.28 a year (the year starting on the holder's birthday), held as charged by the year; it's a maximum (the insurance contribution in it falls with fewer demerit points, and the 2026 rebate the SAAQ announced isn't applied). The probationary licence ($107.96 for 24 months), the learner's licence ($88.35) and the tests aren't held. The page gives no term for the regular licence, so it is null. The SAAQ issues no identity card; licences from outside Quebec weren't read into an exchange list.

sources.said: Before you can hold a full Class 5 driver’s licence, you must first obtain a Class 5 learner's licence (which you must hold for 12 months), pass the driving course, pass the SAAQ's knowledge and road tests, and then hold a Class 5 probationary licence for 24 months. ... be at least 16 years of age ... Last update: September 9, 2026
